summary:
S. 4663, the "Florida Freeze Disaster Assistance Act," appropriates funds for the Secretary of Agriculture to provide block grants to States to compensate for agricultural losses resulting from specified freeze or cold weather conditions.

Section 1 designates the Act's short title.

Section 2 appropriates $3,500,000,000, out of any money in the Treasury not otherwise appropriated, for the fiscal year ending September 30, 2027, as an additional amount for "Agricultural Programs--Office of the Secretary." The appropriation is to remain available until expended. The Secretary of Agriculture is directed to use these funds to provide assistance in the form of block grants to States for losses of revenue, quality, or production of crops (including crops prevented from planting), trees, bushes, and vines caused by a freeze or cold weather condition.

The section includes several provisos conditioning the use of funds. First, the assistance must include compensation to producers for losses of multi-year crops. Second, funds are available exclusively for losses occurring in counties that received a disaster designation for freeze and related cold weather conditions issued by the Secretary on March 4, 2026. Third, funds are made available only upon the request of a State department of agriculture or other appropriate State agency, as determined by the Secretary.

The section imposes a reporting requirement: not later than 120 days after the date of enactment, and for each fiscal quarter thereafter until the funds are expended, the Secretary must submit a report to the House and Senate Committees on Appropriations describing the implementation of the assistance.

Finally, the appropriated amount is designated by Congress as an emergency requirement pursuant to section 251(b)(2)(A)(i) of the Balanced Budget and Emergency Deficit Control Act of 1985 (2 U.S.C. 901(b)(2)(A)(i)).
